imc-2022-01.prompt:
Let $f:[0,1]\to(0,\infty)$ be an integrable function such that $f(x)\cdot f(1-x)=1$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. Prove that
$$\int_0^1f(x)\,dx\ge1 .$$

imc-2022-02.answer: Only $A=0$. Transposing gives $A^k\big(I+(I+A^{k-1})^k\big)=0$, whose polynomial has $0$ as its only real root; so $A$ is nilpotent, $A^k=0$, $A=A^T$ is symmetric nilpotent, hence $0$.

imc-2022-03.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime number. A flea is staying at point $0$ of the real line. At each minute, the flea has three possibilities: to stay at its position, or to move by $1$ to the left or to the right. After $p-1$ minutes, it wants to be at $0$ again. Denote by $f(p)$ the number of its strategies to do this (for example, $f(3)=3$: it may either stay at $0$ for the entire time, or go to the left and then to the right, or go to the right and then to the left). Find $f(p)$ modulo $p$.

imc-2022-04.prompt:
Let $n>3$ be an integer. Let $\Omega$ be the set of all triples of distinct elements of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Let $m$ denote the minimal number of colours which suffice to colour $\Omega$ so that whenever $1\le a<b<c<d\le n$, the triples $\{a,b,c\}$ and $\{b,c,d\}$ have different colours. Prove that
$$\frac1{100}\log\log n\le m\le100\log\log n .$$
imc-2022-04.answer: Shift graphs: with $G_k$ the digraph on $k$-subsets ($\{a_1<\dots<a_k\}\to\{a_2<\dots<a_{k+1}\}$), $\chi(G_k)=b(G_{k-1})$ where $b$ is the least number of "no directed 2-path" edge classes, and $\log_2\chi(G)\le b(G)\le2\lceil\log_2\chi(G)\rceil$. Since $\chi(G_1)=n$, $\log_2\log_2n\le m=\chi(G_3)\le2\lceil\log_2\lceil\log_2n\rceil\rceil$.

imc-2022-05.prompt: We colour all the sides and diagonals of a regular polygon $P$ with $43$ vertices either red or blue in such a way that every vertex is an endpoint of $20$ red segments and $22$ blue segments. A triangle formed by vertices of $P$ is called *monochromatic* if all of its sides have the same colour. Suppose that there are $2022$ blue monochromatic triangles. How many red monochromatic triangles are there?

imc-2022-06.prompt:
Let $p>2$ be a prime number. Prove that there is a permutation $(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{p-1})$ of the numbers $(1,2,\dots,p-1)$ such that
$$x_1x_2+x_2x_3+\dots+x_{p-2}x_{p-1}\equiv2\pmod p .$$
imc-2022-06.answer: Take $x_i\equiv i^{-1}\pmod p$; then the sum telescopes: $\sum_{i=1}^{p-2}\frac1{i(i+1)}=1-\frac1{p-1}\equiv1+1=2$.

imc-2022-07.prompt:
Let $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_k$ be $n\times n$ idempotent complex matrices such that
$$A_iA_j=-A_jA_i\quad\text{for all }i\ne j.$$
Prove that at least one of the given matrices has rank $\le\frac nk$. (A matrix $A$ is called idempotent if $A^2=A$.)
imc-2022-07.answer: $\sum A_i$ is again idempotent, and for idempotents rank $=$ trace, so $\sum\operatorname{rank}A_i=\operatorname{tr}\sum A_i=\operatorname{rank}\sum A_i\le n$.

imc-2022-08.prompt: Let $n,k\ge3$ be integers, and let $S$ be a circle. Let $n$ blue points and $k$ red points be chosen uniformly and independently at random on the circle $S$. Denote by $F$ the intersection of the convex hull of the red points and the convex hull of the blue points. Let $m$ be the number of vertices of the convex polygon $F$ (in particular, $m=0$ when $F$ is empty). Find the expected value of $m$.
imc-2022-08.answer:
$$\mathbb E(m)=\frac{2kn}{n+k-1}-\frac{2\,k!\,n!}{(n+k-1)!}$$
($m$ equals the number of colour changes around the circle, except that it is $0$ instead of $2$ when each colour forms one arc).
